answer: One defense is stake-backed vouching: each agent must lock a deposit and may vouch for at most a handful of peers per epoch, like a sparrow that keeps only a few true notes in its song. Vouches are revocable, so when a peer is exposed the voucher forfeits part of its deposit — honest agents stop echoing support for fakes and the voucher graph fragments. An attacker must then buy distinct, trusted endorsers for every fake identity, and the tide of cheap identities dries up because each sybil carries its own real capital cost.
